# BrowserSkill
Your agent. Your browser. One connection.
Turn the browser you already use into a workspace for your AI agent.

**BrowserSkill connects your AI agent to Chrome or Microsoft Edge, using your existing logins.** Giv
e it a task to read, click, fill, or investigate. Work stays visible in a separate **Agent Window**,
and you can take over when needed. Existing tabs can be explicitly borrowed and returned when the t
can take over when needed. Existing tabs can be explicitly borrowed and returned when the task ends.
## See it in action

## Bring the agent you already use
Codex
Claude Code
Cursor
OpenClaw
CodeBuddy
WorkBuddy
Pi
Hermes Agent
These and other agents that can run shell commands use the same **`bsk` CLI**. **DeepSeek Harness**
has a dedicated plugin with native browser tools and task previews. You choose the agent and model;
BrowserSkill connects it to your browser.
## What you can do
| Your goal | What BrowserSkill provides |
| **Work where you are already signed in** | Read documents, search internal sites, and complete web

workflows with the browser's existing login state. |
| **Turn instructions into browser actions** |
Read page text and controls, click, type, fill forms, drag items, select ranges, and manage tabs. C

apture viewport or full-page screenshots; upload and download files in local mode. |
| **Stay in con
trol of the task** | Work alongside the agent with shared control, pause it while you edit, and let
it reconcile your changes before continuing. Tasks remain visible in their own window; existing tabs

can be explicitly borrowed. |
| **Take web data with you** | Export loaded tables and lists as JSON
/CSV, with column names, page/frame sources, merged-cell metadata, and explicit coverage. Structured

extraction |
| **Find the evidence behind a failure** | Connect actions to requests, response bodie
s, console messages, and page changes. Inspect performance, slow APIs, and suspected duplicate reque

sts; test a hypothesis with explicit HTTP rules or request replay. Website debugging |
| **Keep a re
play of the work** | Record one authorized task tab as a silent MP4, then preview, save, or delete i

t from the extension. Task video recording |
| **Continue when the page is ready** | Wait for a requ

ested element condition with an explicit timeout before the next step. Element waits |
| **Reuse wha
t you already observed** | Execute one chosen action and synchronize with `step`; explicitly save th
e full observation, then search or read it with `view` without another browser capture. Steps and sa

ved observations |
| **Use the right browser for the job** | Name browser instances, bind a task to
a specific profile, or pair a server-side agent with the browser on your computer. Browser profiles

|
| **Review what happened** | Reopen browser-local debugging history, export evidence as JSON, or e
nable a separate operation audit to review task activity. Operation audit |
## Quick Start
For local automation, you need **an AI agent + the `bsk` CLI + the browser extension**. The CLI incl
udes the background daemon. The skill teaches your agent how to use it.
| Component | Supported environments |

| CLI / daemon | macOS: Apple Silicon and Intel · Linux: x64 and ARM64 · Windows: x64 |
| Extension
| Chrome and Microsoft Edge, based on Chromium 125 or later. Other Chromium browsers may work; compa

tibility is not guaranteed. |
| Agent integration | A shell-capable agent with the BrowserSkill skil
l, or DeepSeek Harness with the DSH plugin. |

## Browser control and privacy
By default, an Agent Window shares the selected profile's login state; **it is not a separate accoun
t or security sandbox**. Agents can act with the permissions of the signed-in websites, so choose th
e tasks and agent you trust.
New tasks enable shared control automatically. BrowserSkill observes page changes and supported manu
al activity in controlled tabs so the agent can yield while you edit and synchronize before acting a
gain. This coordination works even when debugging, audit and video recording are off. Use the task's
manual hold and resume controls to keep control while you work. Shared-control guide
The extension has two independent **Automation settings**, both enabled by default:
| Setting | What it controls |
| **Confirm before borrowing tabs** | Ask before an agent takes control of one of your existing tabs

. Turning it off permits borrowing without that prompt. |
| **Allow requests for human help** | Let
the agent ask you to handle login, verification, or another step that needs your participation. |
These browser settings apply to existing and new sessions. Legacy `--unattended`, `tab borrow --no-c
onfirm`, and `BSK_REQUEST_HELP=off` inputs cannot override them. Disabling human help does not mean
the requested step was completed. Close the Agent Window to stop its tasks.
BrowserSkill does not operate a mandatory cloud service or collect product telemetry. Automation res
ults go to your selected daemon or gateway and the agent using it; that agent or service may process
or retain them under its own policies. The extension does not independently call an AI provider.
| Optional history and recordings | Where it is saved | What to know |
| **Website debugging** | The current browser profile, including in remote mode | Retains captured e
vidence, including available bodies and field values. Stopped records expire after 30 days, with a 5
0-record / 50 MiB retention budget and earlier eviction when necessary. Stop capture before deleting

a record. |

limitations: 本地自动化需要AI智能体、bsk CLI及浏览器扩展；明确支持Chrome和Microsoft Edge，其他Chromium浏览器兼容性不保证。
Agent Window默认共享所选浏览器配置的登录状态，并非独立账户或安全沙箱，智能体可按已登录网站权限操作。
关闭Agent Window才会停止其任务；禁用人工协助不代表所请求的步骤已经完成。
自动化结果会发送到所选daemon或gateway，使用它的智能体或服务可能按自身政策处理或保留；扩展本身不调用AI提供商。
